entries.title: Session log started, at the user's direction
entries.lead: The user asked for a standing instruction so future sessions keep a timestamped log, including records of how they directed the agent through prompts, as a helpful record for building the talk.

entries.title: Build the workflow one rule at a time, starting with the prompts
entries.lead: The user asked to start implementing WORKFLOW.md, but explicitly not all at once: first list the rules the workflow will have, then implement the first one and test it, then stop for review before proceeding.

entries.title: Fix the octmnist collision rather than exempt it
entries.lead: Asked to fix the octmnist issue reported at the end of the previous turn, and to see a rendered prompt file in the session rather than only on disk.

entries.title: Smoke next, and show the artifacts in the chat
entries.lead: The user asked for stage 0 next, and for representative artifacts and rule code to be linked in the session afterwards so that readiness for the next stage can be judged without hunting through the repository.

entries.title: Stage 1, and the storage links as a script rather than a rule
entries.lead: Asked to proceed to the next step, which the rule list puts at sampledataset. Two choices in it are worth recording because neither is settled by WORKFLOW.md.

entries.title: The probe, and a workspace that disappeared underneath it
entries.lead: Asked to continue, which the rule list puts at the probe.

entries.title: Runs move to the owner's checkout
entries.lead: Asked to make sure the workflow runs from the persistent filesystem. It was worth checking what that meant: every path involved is on the same /project/dane2 mount, so nothing here is about disks.

entries.title: Thin classes: keep the sample, document the limit
entries.lead: The user asked whether stratifying was not simply cheap and analysis-neutral. It is cheap; it is not neutral, and it is not one thing.

entries.title: Go for the fan-out, and what the first chunk caught
entries.lead: The user said go for the 270-job fan-out.

entries.title: Literature benchmarks, pulled and cited, not rerun
entries.lead: "I would like to pull results from the literature on these particular med mnist tasks and verify and add them as benchmarks in the paper. I don't want to rerun those results.

entries.title: A fifth arm, asked for after the results: the bank in the prompt
entries.lead: "I know it's not clean but I want to try an arm who we ask for a classification zero shot that we give all the concept information.

entries.title: Arm D landed, and two estimates that were wrong
entries.lead: The run finished at 09:34, exit 0. Asked mid-run to estimate the total time, I gave 08:45–08:55 and it took until 09:34.

entries.title: Analysis stops here; attention turns to the talk
entries.lead: "I think we have sufficient results for the talk.

entries.title: Stepping back: the question was about understanding, not substitution
entries.lead: "I think I was more interested in the question, 'to what extent do VLMs understand visual features needed for medical image classification?' This is partly motivated by replacing labeled data, but also simply out of…

entries.title: Does thinking work, can we try an OpenAI model, and the service docs
entries.lead: Three directions in one turn. "Were we able to get thinking to work? Looking at the rcd docs, most of these models should support thinking.

entries.title: Scrub arm D, and propose a thinking arm and an OpenAI arm
entries.lead: "Can you propose how we could integrate a thinking arm and an openai arm, on more limited cases to keep overall calls relatively low while still giving bite?

entries.title: H4 joins the hypotheses, at medium effort, and the build goes out
entries.lead: "Join the hypotheses in workflow. Let's do medium.

entries.title: "What's left to run?" — and what the answer turned up
entries.lead: The user asked for a status.

entries.title: The talk plan, fixed: workflow first, H4 as the follow-on
entries.lead: "I would like to take your original talk plan and basically keep it. I don't want the talk to center around the hypothesis but the workflow, the basic spirit of the problem we're solving and what the evidence says.

entries.title: The H4 chain lands; the talk's scene 6 stands
entries.lead: No prompt. The run launched at 17:42 under the cap of four finished at 21:40, 40 of 40, with every thinking chunk complete and no cell flagged.

entries.title: Embeddings, and the redirect to the service's own embedding model
entries.lead: "I would like to try using embeddings. Add this in in a principled fashion, run it, analyze the outputs, and put it in the report.

entries.title: "If the embed API can't take pixels my idea is a no go"
entries.lead: Checked at the wire rather than from the model listing: the embedding model rejects an imageurl input with a validation error, the three OpenAI embedding models are text-only, and the vision chat models are not…

entries.title: "Remove all the nonsense not using pixels. Just rewind."
entries.lead: "This idea doesn't make any sense going through the fingerprints." Done.

entries.title: Cleaning audit: everything the talk needs, and only that
entries.lead: "Now that the workflow is set and all results are in, perform a cleaning audit to make sure we have everything needed and only everything needed for the talk workflow.

entries.title: "Restore the txt rule. Update and recompile the tex. You can delete the D results"
entries.lead: All three decisions the audit had left open, answered in one line.

entries.title: "Why don't I have a hypothesis that compares ... with zero shot?"
entries.lead: The owner asked why no hypothesis sets the concept regression (arm C) against zero-shot (arm A); the answer - the plan paired arms by label budget, and H2's result made A the zero-label line that matters after the fact…

entries.title: "Expand the full analysis to all 12 MedMNIST. Follow it through from start to finish."
entries.lead: "I know this is a long request that will involve many calls. Proceed until complete and documented." The talk version's six datasets become the twelve 2D benchmarks, the whole workflow run to the report.

entries.title: Twelve datasets, start to finish, complete
entries.lead: The expansion asked for at 08:20 ran to the report in under two hours of wall clock: four fetches in a minute each, six samples, 227 chunks in 66 minutes on an uncontended Sunday service, the analysis chain for twelve…

entries.title: "Hypothesize that P + C beats P. Register the hypothesis, then run it and integrate it"
entries.lead: Asked alongside a question about whether the study is publishable (answered in the session, with the literature search behind it).

entries.title: A second session on the same task, and the damage it did
entries.lead: A second Claude session was given the P + C prompt at 11:45 without the owner intending two to run at once, and did not know the 10:40 session existed.

entries.title: H5 run and integrated, after a concurrent session disturbed the run
entries.lead: The hypothesis registered at 10:40 ran and is supported: 11 of 12, p = 0.0032, every winning interval clear of zero, median gain 0.007 AUC.

entries.title: An accuracy pass over the report, and the prompts as an appendix
entries.lead: Asked to take a pass through the report for accuracy, add anything specific to the analysis that had been left out, add appendices showing the prompts, and make sure arm C+P's fusion is described.

entries.title: Arm C+P on the learning curve, and a sampled-image appendix
entries.lead: Two asks. First, put H5's arm on the plot of performance against number of training samples.

entries.title: Four questions about the frontier reader, none of them bought
entries.lead: Asked whether the frontier model might be overthinking, whether to try luna, terra and sol at the lowest effort, whether the API offers astra, and whether the credits stretch to it.

entries.title: "Test the reasoning level idea on terra. Test the model capabilities at low reasoning for Luna, terra, and Sol"
entries.lead: Approved after the costing of the previous turn, and with the caveat standing that the credit balance cannot be read from here — the service has no endpoint for it, so this is the owner's approved spend rather than a…

entries.title: H6 and H7 decided
entries.lead: Both ran to the report in about seventy minutes and cost $38.76 at list, $19.38 at flex, under the $53.59 / $26.79 quoted before the owner approved it. Findings are in CHANGELOG.md.

entries.title: A hyperlinked contents page
entries.lead: Asked for one, and the report had grown to seventy-four pages, so it earned it. Three things had to change beyond adding \tableofcontents.

entries.title: Visuals for H6 and H7
entries.lead: Two figures, each shaped by what its hypothesis has to show rather than by reusing the forest plot the report already has twice.

entries.title: "Clean up hanging checkouts or branches that were never merged in"
entries.lead: The ask: one clean lineage for the talk, everything accounted for, and results that are always in the owner's checkout rather than somewhere a future session left them.

entries.title: "The talk as a website: science as the spine, reproducibility as callouts"
entries.lead: The talk is no longer a deck.

entries.title: Three reviews of the talk site, implemented
entries.lead: The user had the talk website read by three reviewers — one for the visuals, one for the text, one for the presentation flow — and handed the agent their merged, prioritised change list to implement, with the editorial…

entries.title: The opening re-cut: the method is the talk, the study is the demonstration
entries.lead: The user began a batch of copy edits on the talk site, delivered in conversation rather than as review comments on a branch, and the first batch moved the talk's centre of gravity.

entries.title: A byline under the title
entries.lead: The user asked for their name and department under the talk's title: D. Hudson Smith, School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences.

entries.title: Presenter mode bulletises the prose
entries.lead: The user asked presenter mode to crunch the longer prose blocks into a few skimmable bullets: points the room takes in at a glance, and a reminder of the speaker's own flow, with the sentences said out loud rather than…

entries.title: Presenter mode becomes a deck
entries.lead: The user raised the ask: in presenter mode the site should read almost as slides — one main section per screen, text collapsed to bullets, the visual and its text together, the title prominent, everything in chunks…

entries.title: The slides come back out
entries.lead: The user tried the deck and rejected the constraint: "the slides idea appears to be too difficult a constraint on differently sized screens." Fixed 100vh panels assume a projector's aspect ratio and punish every other…

entries.title: The callout legend comes out, and the calls go in
entries.lead: Two edits in one pass. The user cut the premise's "Three kinds of callout" legend — "too on the nose.

entries.title: Replace the four-day strip with a waterfall of who did the work
entries.lead: The user found TimelineStrip inscrutable and asked for a waterfall instead: two bands over the same axis, project-lifecycle activity in one and human against AI against supercomputer time in the other, to convey that…

entries.title: Inside baseball comes off the page
entries.lead: The user quoted the effort figure's caveat paragraph back and said to remove it "and any such 'inside baseball' comments from the website".

entries.title: One mode, and it is the talk
entries.lead: The user read the effort chart's text summary, found it a wall, and drew the general conclusion: "This is primarily a talk. Not a complete documentation of the project.

entries.title: Say the thing instead of gesturing at it
entries.lead: The user named the failure mode with an example: "'The shape of the thing' is just so vague.

entries.title: Not a waterfall: a project timeline, with points where there are no durations
entries.lead: The user's verdict on the two-band waterfall was that "waterfall" had been the wrong word, and that what he wanted was a project-timeline Gantt: named steps as lanes down the left, one clock across the top, a bar…

entries.title: Surface the RCD LLM service calls, at the resolution the archive supports
entries.lead: The user asked whether the calls to the RCD LLM service could be highlighted as events. They are the largest number the study produced and they were invisible, folded inside the bars for the jobs that made them.

entries.title: The figures get the plain-language pass, and "checklist" loses its place
entries.lead: The prose had been through a plain-language pass and the figures had not, so the same standard was carried inside them: axis labels, legend entries, direct end-labels, in-figure annotations, column headers drawn in…

entries.title: The owner's edits, distilled and applied
entries.lead: The user edited the talk's text directly, then asked for the principles behind those edits to be carried through the rest of it. Reading the diff, four rules: 1. Bullets carry facts; callouts carry observations.

entries.title: Motivate the science first
entries.lead: The user found the opening out of order: "what is the 4 days of work 58,409 number etc. Right after the title...

entries.title: The hypotheses leave the talk
entries.lead: The user cut the pre-registration walkthrough: "hypotheses as tiles doesn't really work. List them out. Also, for the sake of time, let's not pre-register the hypotheses at all.

entries.title: MedMNIST first, then the textbook, then a duplication sweep
entries.lead: The user recast the section that had been called What we asked the model: name it "Medical images and associated visual features", make it MedMNIST-focused, describe the dataset in the bullets, and centre the second…

entries.title: The talk cut to twenty-five minutes
entries.lead: Overnight instructions, in the order they arrived: the talk is far too long; the learning curve should be the headline, with a control that picks which question you are asking and presets the arms that answer it; keep…

entries.title: The classifiers are not identical, and the models get a section
entries.lead: Three instructions, in the order they arrived. "The classifiers are not identical.

entries.title: Titles that name their contents
entries.lead: The user cut a panel and named a habit. The panel — "How many calls each model answered, and under what name" — repeated the models table three sections above it, so it went.

entries.title: Name the model behind every result
entries.lead: Naming the model under the results figure turned out to be an instance of a rule: "Everywhere we report a result that depends on model outputs, you should clarify what model is used." Every section was pulled off the…

entries.title: A plain-language pass over all the copy
entries.lead: The user asked for the standard he has been applying by hand for two days to be carried through every line on the site: "avoid vague terminology, unusual metaphors, virtue signaling.

entries.title: "Checklist" goes, and seven callouts with it
entries.lead: Two instructions, one pass. The first: "I don't like 'checklist'. Plain language issue. Use 'visual features' or 'feature scores', 'scored visual features'. Apply throughout. Identify other similar vagueness.

entries.title: It is the scholarly record, not a textbook; and the talk ends on takeaways
entries.lead: Nine instructions in one batch, and the first is a factual correction rather than a style one: "Calling it textbook features is not quite right. These features were scraped from over 100 scientific papers.

entries.title: The fourteen label collisions, and what a collision actually is
entries.lead: The sweep that ended the last entry was measuring the wrong thing.

entries.title: The takeaways are a deck, and the agent's three are gone
entries.lead: "Remove this callout. And these points." The Understanding debt note and the three bullets the agent had proposed under its own heading are cut; what the section carries now is his ten, and only his.

entries.title: "The compute workflow", and why a workflow manager at all
entries.lead: Section five is The compute workflow now, in the heading and in the rail, and the two paragraphs explaining make are replaced by the argument he actually wants made there: what a workflow manager is worth when an agent…

entries.title: The archived call is its own section, and carries the questions
entries.lead: "'One archived image, and both answers'. First of all, this language is too indirect. Secondly, this is orphaned." Both true.

entries.title: Four lines and a logo; the heading stands alone; what the bands are
entries.lead: Three corrections in quick succession, all in the same direction: less.

entries.title: Why four of the twelve lines carry a name
entries.lead: "Why were path, pneumonia, organa, organs highlighted here? I'm fine with it.

entries.title: The logo goes
entries.lead: "Looks bad." It did: the wordmark was set in a face and weight nothing else on the page uses, on a line with a sentence it was neither part of nor clearly separate from, and in dark mode it was an inverted grey that…

entries.title: "in its place" said nothing
entries.lead: "What do you mean by 'and then gpt-5.6-terra in its place'?" Fair question, and the answer is the thing the sentence failed to say.

entries.title: Five corrections to the thinking section, and a tic named
entries.lead: "You keep using this pattern: 'Two steps, one change each.' Stop!

kind_note: Only the kind of each entry was assigned by hand; the rest is the file's own heading and first paragraph.
